rappel_detail.notes: First rappel off the ridge crest working down toward the notch by the large chockstone that marks the top of the descent gully.
rappel_detail.anchor: Slung horn/chockstone near West Ridge crest

rappel_detail.notes: Second rappel finishing the ridge-crest section; some parties do only one here and downclimb/simul-downclimb the rest.
First rappel down the loose, rockfall-prone gully into Crescent Creek Basin; a single 50-60m rope is sufficient for every reported station.
rappel_detail.anchor: Natural chockstone/horn anchor in the descent gully

rappel_detail.notes: Final gully rappel; the last ~100 ft below this is loose and marginal and is downclimbed.

set.rappels: About 4 rappels on a single 60 m rope down the West Ridge descent: one or two near the ridge crest above the notch, then two or three in the loose gully to Crescent Creek Basin. Parties report 3-5 rappels depending on snow and how much they downclimb.
set.descent: Descend the West Ridge to the notch above the descent gully, then rappel and downclimb the gully into Crescent Creek Basin.
gear: Single set of cams from roughly 0.3 to 3 inches, doubled in the 1-2 inch range for the crux
A 60 m rope for the rappel descent; one is enough for every reported station
Ice axe and crampons if snow/ice cover the approach gully or ridge, common in early season
Helmet — the rock here is notably loose
Extra slings and lockers for tat or fixed rappel anchors
